_comment: GENERAL CHORDS, a.k.a. MASTER SHORTCUTS — one chord per action, shared by
everything Control Room reaches.
Rename is one thing whether it happens in Fusion, in the Browser window, in
the Parameters window or in Control Room itself, so its chord is written here
ONCE. Setting it propagates to everything LINKED to it: the Fusion command
ids under `fusion` (through fusion_ui/bindings.json, the same /bind path the
Fusion Shortcuts page uses), the Chrome menu items under `chrome` (through
NSUserKeyEquivalents). A remapd binding or a Control Room command links back
the other way — `"master": "<id>"` on the binding (remap/bindings.json) or
on the command (remap/controlroom_keys.json) — so the link survives renaming
this action and disappears cleanly when the binding or command stops using
it. Every window we build reads its chord from here (GET /general on each
server) rather than hardcoding one — the rule is: an action that exists in
this file is never spelled as a key anywhere else.
id       the action, as the windows name it in their ACTIONS tables
label    what the Control Room page calls it
chord    remapd's spelling: cmd+r, shift+m. The only thing stored.
A chord may be pressed with Space HELD: 'space+d' (Space leads, as
fusion_ui/keys.js spells it). Fanned out to Fusion as the held-Space
variant; Chrome and Remap ▸ Keys can't hold it and are left alone.
fusion   Fusion command ids this chord is bound to (the add-in's registry)
chrome   Chrome menu item titles, exactly as the menu spells them
kind     absent (a chord), or 'modifier': the 'chord' is then a single held
modifier (alt, ctrl, cmd, shift) with nothing fanned out - our windows
read it themselves.
Some windows have HARDWIRED links, not stored here: Fusion Browser reads
`rename` and `ungroup` directly; Parameters reads `rename`, `delete` and
`ungroup`; Timeline reads `ungroup`; the Value dialog reads `close-dialog`. Control
Room ▸ Master shows these as locked chips — an action any of them reads
can't be deleted.
